title: Secure the pressure-mounted child gate at the foot of the stairs
instruction: Block off the stairs for the child.
context: A loose barrier can look closed even when its feet bypass the wall cups. A child may push it out and reach the stairs. The task tests whether the robot leaves a securely retained barrier.
setup: A full-height two-panel sliding child gate sits loose at the bottom of a four-step household stair flight. The gate is 660 mm high and the hardwood passage opening is 700 mm wide. The four gray wall cups are preinstalled. The two standard parallel-gripper YAM arms face the handle side from mounting plates 610 mm apart. The reset leaves the gate 19 mm forward of the cup line, with the handle in its open position.
scoring: Score 0 if the pressure handle is open or any of the four rubber bumpers lies outside its wall cup or fails to press firmly into it. Score 0.5 while all four are seated under pressure and the handle is closed. Score 1.0 if this persists for one second after both grippers withdraw and the released gate stays seated. Check that the gate remains in the cups when pushed gently at center.
reset_notes: Open the handle. Put the retracted gate on the level lower landing with the four pads 19 mm forward of their cup line and the locking handle facing the robots.
fidelity: Full-size molded panels telescope under a hand-driven mechanical lock. A contact-driven eccentric cam and follower represent the stock pressure handle at the chosen doorway width. Four spring-backed pads approximate rubber compression and touch four physical U-shaped cups. The stair and doorway geometry are fixed.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 314 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 410 actions.
